trust_decision.summary: The JSON object_hook in my_load_from_json decides which Python class a '__type__' [module, class] pair may instantiate; at the pinned commit it imports any module and calls any attribute with the remaining keys as kwargs.

landing_point.why: The summary names JSON deserialization and '__type__'; the only '__type__' handler in the tree is __object_hook in my_load_from_json.

fix_sites.entry_point: module-level allowlist JSON_SERIALIZABLE (fix.diff:21-22), consulted by my_load_from_json
@serializable decorator, run at import time on every serializable class (fix.diff:31-33); registers JsonSerializable subclasses
my_load_from_json / JsonSerializable.load_from_json / JsonSerializable.load_from_json_file (public API) and REST API BaseHandler.load_json_data_from_request (HTTP request bodies)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Every caller goes through the one my_load_from_json function: REST (epyt_flow/rest_api/base_handler.py:67) and file/str API (epyt_flow/serialization.py:325, epyt_flow/serialization.py:343). ScenarioConfig.load_from_json (epyt_flow/simulation/scenario_config.py:495-711) is a separate JSON loader, but it uses plain json.loads with a closed string->class mapping (scenario_config.py:593-602, 659-664, 674-685), so it is not a vulnerable second implementation.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is little to dismiss, because every route funnels through one hook. A solver could argue the msgpack loader (epyt_flow/serialization.py:66-71, 411-442) is a separate format outside the JSON advisory, but it already resolves classes only through the umsgpack ext_serializable ID registry (serialization.py:99), so it needs no change.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Round-tripping registered JsonSerializable objects (my_to_json emits '__type__' = (obj.__module__, class name)) and plain dicts with no '__type__' (most REST bodies, e.g. kwargs for scenario creation) must keep working. An over-broad fix that rejects every '__type__', or keys the allowlist differently from what the serializer emits, breaks REST event/control/uncertainty uploads and to_json/load_from_json round trips.

O6_input_shapes: __type__ as JSON list [module, class] (the normal shape)
__type__ with wrong length or non-string elements (rejected with ValueError)
__type__ naming a class outside the registered JsonSerializable set (rejected)
falsy/empty __type__ (passed through as a plain dict)
nested typed objects (json object_hook processes inner dicts first)

O7_producer.where: epyt_flow/serialization.py:251-254 (my_to_json writes '__type__'); the allowlist is filled by the @serializable decorator at epyt_flow/serialization.py:88-99 at import time

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A config-file 'type' dispatcher in ScenarioConfig.load_from_json that resolves uncertainty/leak/fault classes by dotted name via importlib instead of the closed if/elif map
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding pluggable custom uncertainty or event classes to JSON scenario configs would plausibly swap the hard-coded map for dynamic import. It sits in another package (simulation) and never calls my_load_from_json.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A msgpack ext handler that decodes a class or dtype reference by name (e.g. an ext type that carries a [module, class] pair for custom user objects)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The ext handler table is already extended for numpy, networkx and scipy, so a generic 'any object' ext handler is a natural addition and moves the same mechanism into the binary format.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second REST body parser (e.g. a form/multipart or falcon media handler) that does its own '__type__' resolution
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The REST layer has about 19 handlers calling load_json_data_from_request. A maintainer adding file upload support might write a local parser. But this is a WHERE-type sibling, which lessons say is cheap to find.

O9_family: CWE-502 unsafe deserialization (polymorphic type resolution from attacker-controlled JSON '__type__')

O10_build.toolchain: pip / setuptools (pure-Python package; depends on umsgpack, numpy, networkx, scipy, falcon, and epanet_plus, which ships EPANET native libs)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_serialization.py (msgpack round trips), tests/test_configparser.py:51 (ScenarioConfig.load_from_json). There is no direct test of my_load_from_json / '__type__' at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Restrict '__type__' module names to the 'epyt_flow.' prefix (still allows any callable attribute of any epyt_flow module) instead of an explicit registry of JsonSerializable classes.

out_of_scope_notes: Allowlisted classes still take arbitrary kwargs from JSON (cls(**args)); whether any registered class constructor has dangerous side effects was not examined.
REST scenario creation passes JSON kwargs straight to scenario_mgr.create(**args) (epyt_flow/rest_api/scenario/handlers.py:190-191); its file-path handling is a separate concern.
unverified: repo_mb unknown: no shell to measure size, so tiny_repo was neither confirmed nor ruled out (package source looks small, so a tiny_repo red flag is likely).

single_site is not listed: the fix changes two functions plus a module constant in one file, so the strict definition does not hold. In effect the host behaves as a single-site fix (one hook, every route funnels through it).
regression_tests_in_pinned_commit not applicable: the fix diff adds no test files.

DeepGaussianUncertainty (epyt_flow/uncertainty/uncertainties.py:447) is JsonSerializable but not @serializable-decorated, so it is not registered after the fix. It appears to be an abstract base, but whether it is ever JSON round-tripped directly was not checked.
